summary: The mitzvah of covering the blood (kisui hadam) after shechting a wild animal or a bird applies everywhere and always, but not for korbanos. For a koy, which may be a farm animal or a wild one, we cover the blood because of the doubt.

chunks.he: כִּסּוּי הַדָּם נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: Covering the blood applies in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.explain: After shechting a wild animal or bird, we cover its blood with earth.
chunks.st: The mitzva of covering the blood after slaughter is in effect both in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael, both

chunks.en: when the Beis HaMikdash stands and when it does not,
chunks.st: in the presence, i.e., the time, of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple.

chunks.en: with plain animals, but not with korbanos.
chunks.st: And it is in effect with regard to non-sacred animals, but it is not in effect with regard to sacrificial ones.

chunks.en: And it applies to wild animals and to birds,
chunks.st: And it is in effect with regard to the slaughter of an undomesticated animal and a bird,

chunks.en: those kept at home and those that are not.
chunks.st: with regard to animals and birds that are readily available in his home, and with regard to those that are not readily available and are hunted in the wild.

words.en: and to those that are not

chunks.en: And it applies to a koy,
chunks.explain: A koy is an animal we are not sure is a farm animal or a wild one.
chunks.st: And it is in effect with regard to a koy,

chunks.en: because it is a doubt.
chunks.st: because it is uncertain
chunks.stMore: whether a koy is a domesticated animal and one is exempt from the covering of its blood or whether it is an undomesticated animal and one is obligated to cover it.

chunks.en: And we may not shecht it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: And one may not slaughter a koy on a Festival,
chunks.stMore: because covering its blood entails the performance of prohibited labor that is permitted only if there is a definite obligation to cover the blood.

chunks.en: And if he shechted it,
chunks.st: And if one slaughtered a koy on a Festival after the fact,

chunks.en: we do not cover its blood.
chunks.st: one does not cover its blood until after the Festival.

summary: If the shechitah did not make the meat allowed, Rabbi Meir says we still must cover the blood, and the Sages say we do not. If the shechitah was not done properly at all, there is no mitzvah to cover.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts and it turns out to be a treifah,
chunks.st: In the case of one who slaughters an undomesticated animal or a bird and it is discovered to be an animal with a wound that would have caused it to die within twelve months [tereifa];

chunks.en: or who shechts for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: and in the case of one who slaughters an undomesticated animal or a bird for the sake of idol worship;

chunks.en: or who shechts a plain animal inside the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: and in the case of one who slaughters a non-sacred animal or bird inside the Temple courtyard

chunks.en: or a korban outside,
chunks.st: or a sacrificial bird outside the Temple courtyard; or in the case of one who slaughters

chunks.en: or a wild animal or bird sentenced to be stoned:
chunks.st: an undomesticated animal or a bird that was sentenced to be stoned,
chunks.stMore: e.g., for killing a person; in all these cases, even though it is prohibited to eat any of these animals or birds,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he must cover,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems one obligated to cover their blood,

chunks.en: and the Sages say he does not need to.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem one exempt from doing so
chunks.stMore: because, in their opinion, slaughter that is not fit to render the meat permitted for consumption is not considered an act of slaughter.

chunks.en: Someone who shechts and it becomes a neveilah in his hand,
chunks.st: One who slaughters an animal or bird and it became a carcass by his hand, i.e., the slaughter was performed incorrectly,

chunks.en: or who stabs it, or who rips out the simanim,
chunks.st: and one who stabs the animal or bird, and one who tears loose the windpipe and the gullet, are

chunks.en: does not need to cover.
chunks.st: exempt from covering the blood,
chunks.stMore: as no act of slaughter took place, and one is obligated to cover blood only after a valid slaughter.

summary: If a deaf-mute, someone not mentally fit, or a child shechted while others watched, the blood must be covered and the shechitah counts for "it and its child". If no one watched, we are not sure it was a real shechitah.

chunks.he: חֵרֵשׁ, שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ וַאֲחֵרִים רוֹאִין אוֹתָן,
chunks.en: A deaf-mute, someone not mentally fit, or a child who shechted while others watch them:
chunks.st: In the case of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor who slaughtered an undomesticated animal or a bird, and others saw them
chunks.stMore: and ensured that the slaughter was properly performed, in which case the slaughter is valid (see 2a), one who oversaw the slaughter is

chunks.en: one must cover the blood.
chunks.st: obligated to cover the blood.

chunks.en: If they were by themselves,
chunks.st: If they slaughtered the animals among themselves without supervision, one is

chunks.en: one does not need to cover.
chunks.st: exempt
chunks.stMore: from the obligation to cover the blood.

chunks.en: And the same with "it and its child":
chunks.st: And likewise with regard to the matter of slaughtering a mother and its offspring on the same day, if a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor

chunks.en: if they shechted while others watch them,
chunks.st: slaughtered an undomesticated mother animal and others saw them, it is

chunks.en: it is forbidden to shecht after them.
chunks.st: prohibited to slaughter its offspring after them.

chunks.en: If they were by themselves,
chunks.st: If they slaughtered the mother animal among themselves,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir allows shechting after them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems it permitted to slaughter its offspring after them

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it prohibited.

chunks.en: And they agree that if he did shecht,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis concede that if one slaughtered the offspring thereafter

chunks.en: he does not get the forty lashes.
chunks.st: that he does not incur the forty lashes,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible the mother was not properly slaughtered.

summary: One covering is enough for the blood of many animals or birds shechted in one place. If someone did not cover the blood, whoever sees it must cover it; if the wind covered it and then it was uncovered, it must still be covered.

chunks.en: If he shechted a hundred wild animals in one place,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered one hundred undomesticated animals in one place,

chunks.en: one covering is enough for all of them.
chunks.st: one covering of the blood suffices for all the animals
chunks.stMore: and there is no obligation to cover the blood of each animal separately. Likewise, if one slaughtered

chunks.en: A hundred birds in one place,
chunks.st: one hundred birds in one place,

chunks.en: one covering for all of them.
chunks.st: one covering of the blood suffices for all the birds. If one slaughtered

chunks.en: A wild animal and a bird in one place,
chunks.st: an undomesticated animal and a bird in one place,

chunks.en: one covering for all of them.
chunks.st: one covering for all of the blood is sufficient.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: If one

chunks.en: If he shechted a wild animal,
chunks.st: slaughtered an undomesticated animal,

chunks.he: יְכַסֶּנָּה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִשְׁחֹט אֶת הָעוֹף.
chunks.en: he should cover it, and afterwards shecht the bird.
chunks.st: he should cover its blood immediately and only thereafter he should slaughter the bird.

chunks.en: If he shechted and did not cover, and someone else saw it,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered an undomesticated animal or bird and did not cover the blood, and another person saw the uncovered blood, the second person is

chunks.en: the other person must cover it.
chunks.st: obligated to cover the blood.

chunks.en: If he covered it and it got uncovered,
chunks.st: If one covered the blood and it was then uncovered, he is

chunks.en: he does not need to cover it again.
chunks.st: exempt from covering it again.

chunks.en: If the wind covered it,
chunks.st: If the wind blew earth on the blood and covered it, and it was consequently uncovered, he is

chunks.en: he must cover it.
chunks.st: obligated to cover the blood.

summary: If the blood got mixed with water and still looks like blood, it must be covered. If it got mixed with wine or other blood, we imagine the wine or other blood is water; Rabbi Yehudah says blood never cancels blood.

chunks.en: Blood that got mixed with water:
chunks.st: In a case of the blood of an undomesticated animal or bird that was mixed with water,

chunks.en: if it still looks like blood,
chunks.st: if there is in the mixture the appearance of blood one is

chunks.en: he must cover it.
chunks.st: obligated to cover it. If the blood

chunks.en: If it got mixed with wine,
chunks.st: was mixed with wine

chunks.en: we look at the wine as if it were water.
chunks.st: one views the wine as though it is water,
chunks.stMore: and if a mixture with that amount of water would have the appearance of blood one is obligated to cover it. Likewise, if the blood of an undomesticated animal or a bird

chunks.he: נִתְעָרֵב בְּדַם הַבְּהֵמָה אוֹ בְדַם הַחַיָּה,
chunks.en: If it got mixed with the blood of a farm animal, or with other blood of the wild animal,
chunks.explain: Other blood that does not need covering.
chunks.st: was mixed with the blood of a domesticated animal, which one does not have to cover, or with blood of the undomesticated animal that did not flow from the neck and does not require covering,

chunks.en: we look at that blood as if it were water.
chunks.st: one views the blood as though it is water.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Blood does not cancel blood.
chunks.st: Blood does not nullify blood.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, even if the undomesticated animal’s blood, which one must cover, is not recognizable in this mixture, he is obligated to cover the mixture nevertheless.

summary: Blood that splashed out or that is on the knife must also be covered. Rabbi Yehudah says that is only when there is no other blood there to cover.

chunks.en: Blood that splashed, and blood that is on the knife,
chunks.st: With regard to blood that spurts outside the pit over which the animal was slaughtered, or onto a wall, and blood that remained on the slaughtering knife, one is

chunks.en: must be covered.
chunks.st: obligated to cover it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין שָׁם דָּם אֶלָּא הוּא.
chunks.en: When? When there is no other blood there except it.
chunks.st: When is this the halakha? When no blood remains there from the slaughter except that blood.

chunks.he: אֲבָל יֵשׁ שָׁם דָּם שֶׁלֹּא הוּא,
chunks.en: But if there is other blood there,
chunks.st: But if blood remains there from the slaughter that is not that blood, he is

chunks.en: he does not need to cover it.
chunks.st: exempt from covering it.

summary: We cover the blood with fine things that plants can grow in, like fine earth or sand. We may not cover it with lumpy things, or just turn a vessel over it.

chunks.en: With what do we cover,
chunks.st: With what substances may one cover the blood

chunks.en: and with what do we not cover?
chunks.st: and with what substances may one not cover the blood?

chunks.en: We cover with fine dung,
chunks.st: One may cover the blood with fine granulated manure,

chunks.en: and with fine sand,
chunks.st: with fine sand,

chunks.en: with lime, and with crushed clay,
chunks.st: with lime, with crushed potsherd,

chunks.en: and with a brick or a jar lid that he crushed.
chunks.st: and with a brick or the lid of an earthenware barrel that one crushed.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אֵין מְכַסִּין לֹא בְזֶבֶל הַגַּס,
chunks.en: But we do not cover with lumpy dung,
chunks.st: But one may not cover the blood with thick manure,

chunks.en: nor with lumpy sand,
chunks.st: nor with thick, clumped sand,

chunks.en: nor with a brick or a jar lid that he did not crush.
chunks.st: nor with a brick or the lid of an earthenware barrel that one did not crush.

chunks.en: And he should not turn a vessel upside down over it.
chunks.st: Neither may one merely turn a vessel over the blood.

chunks.he: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said a rule:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated a principle:

chunks.en: Something that plants can grow in,
chunks.st: With regard to a substance in which plants grow,

chunks.en: we may cover with it.
chunks.st: one may cover blood with it;

chunks.en: And something that plants do not grow in,
chunks.st: and with regard to a substance in which plants do not grow,

chunks.en: we may not cover with it.
chunks.st: one may not cover blood with it.
